Simulate data with deviant within-cluster variances

Source: R/simulate_ivd.R
simulate_ivd.Rd

Simulate MELSM data with known deviant clusters

Usage

simulate_ivd(
  J = 100,
  n_j = 20,
  n_deviant = ceiling(0.05 * J),
  deviant_clusters = NULL,
  deviant_factor = 2,
  beta = 0,
  sigma_within = 1,
  tau_loc = 0.5,
  family = c("gaussian", "student"),
  df = 3,
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

J

Number of clusters. Defaults to 100.

n_j

Observations per cluster: a single number or a length-J vector. Defaults to 20.

n_deviant

Number of deviant clusters, drawn at random. Defaults to 5% of J (rounded up). Ignored when deviant_clusters is given.

deviant_clusters

Optional integer vector of cluster indices to make deviant (overrides n_deviant).

deviant_factor

Multiplicative factor on the within-cluster SD of the deviant clusters: 2 doubles it, 0.5 halves it. A single number or one value per deviant cluster. Defaults to 2.

beta

Location grand mean (fixed intercept). Defaults to 0.

sigma_within

Baseline within-cluster SD of the regular clusters. Defaults to 1. With family = "student" this is the scale of the t (its SD is sigma_within * sqrt(df/(df-2))).

tau_loc

SD of the location random intercepts. Defaults to 0.5.

family

Residual distribution: "gaussian" (default) or "student" for heavy-tailed t residuals with df degrees of freedom -- useful for checking how heavy tails masquerade as variance heterogeneity under a gaussian ivd() fit.

df

Degrees of freedom of the student-t residuals (must be > 2 so the variance exists). Only used with family = "student". Defaults to 3.

seed

Optional seed for reproducibility.

Value

A list of class ivd_sim:

  • data: data frame with y and cluster id, ready for ivd().

  • truth: data frame with one row per cluster: id, u_loc, sd_within, factor, and deviant.

  • params: the simulation parameters.

Details

Generates data from the intercept-only mixed-effects location-scale model that ivd() fits, with a known subset of clusters whose residual (within-cluster) SD deviates from the common baseline: $$y_{ij} = \beta_0 + u_j + e_{ij}, \quad e_{ij} \sim N(0, \sigma_j^2),$$ where \(u_j \sim N(0, \tau_{loc}^2)\) are location random intercepts and \(\sigma_j = \sigma_{within} \cdot f_j\) with \(f_j = 1\) for regular clusters and \(f_j =\) deviant_factor for the deviant ones.

Because the ground truth is known, the output is suited for power analysis (how many clusters/observations to detect a given SD inflation?), teaching, and validating recovery: fit with ivd(y ~ 1 + (1 | id), ~ 1 + (1 | id), data = sim$data, ...) and compare pip(fit) against sim$truth.

Author

Philippe Rast

Examples

sim <- simulate_ivd(J = 20, n_j = 10, n_deviant = 2, seed = 1)
sim
#> Simulated MELSM data: 20 clusters, 200 observations
#>   Baseline within-cluster SD: 1 (location grand mean 0, tau_loc 0.5)
#>   2 deviant cluster(s): 4, 7 (SD factor 2)
#> 
#> Fit with, e.g.:
#>   ivd(y ~ 1 + (1 | id), ~ 1 + (1 | id), data = <sim>$data, ...)
subset(sim$truth, deviant)
#>   id  n        u_loc sd_within factor deviant
#> 4  4 10 -0.769975021         2      2    TRUE
#> 7  7 10 -0.002883586         2      2    TRUE
if (FALSE) {
fit <- ivd(y ~ 1 + (1 | id), ~ 1 + (1 | id), data = sim$data,
           niter = 2000, nburnin = 2000)
merge(pip(fit), sim$truth, by.x = "cluster_id", by.y = "id")
}
